newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA TO LIBERALISE FOREX MARKET IN TWO MONTHS.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA TO LIBERALISE FOREX MARKET IN TWO MONTHS.

text.p: Romania plans to remove foreign exchange market curbs, by renewing dealer licences to several banks, within the next two months, central bank (BNR) governor Mugur Isarescu said on Thursday.
"The liberalisation will come after parliament approves a new reform package, which should be within two months," Isarescu told Reuters in an interview.
Foreign exchange market curbs, imposed by the former ruling leftists last March, were among reasons which prompted the International Monetary Fund to suspend loan tranches last year.

Romania's new centrist ruling coalition, who toppled ex-communists in last November's elections, has pledged faster reforms including liberalising currency market, now restricted to only four market-making dealer banks.
Besides those four another 16 banks operate on the market.
The move to free the market is a plank under new loan talks with a team of Fund experts expected in Bucharest on Thursday.

Banks operating on Romania's fledgling interbank market must observe the rates imposed by the four selected banks, which had allowed the former leftist administration to keep the local leu artificially high ahead of last year's elections.
"We are taking steps for (the creation of) a functional forex market, but we cannot say where the market will stabilise," Isarescu said.
"We knew that the leu was over-valued, so we have seen a rapid depreciation of the currency."
Over the past month or so the four dealer banks, three of which are state-run, appeared to be more flexible, allowing the leu to edge down to what many traders deem to be a "more realistic value".

Isarescu declined to speculate on the further depreciation of the leu, whose fall against the dollar gathered pace in the past weeks amid rising inflation fears and hammered by a bulging trade deficit estimated at about $2.0 billion.
The leu shed some 20 percent to 4,950/5,050 to the dollar on the interbank market since Janury 1, with traders expecting it to suffer further loses towards 5,200/300 by weekend.
But the leu-dollar interbank rates remained still higher than retail prices which hover now around 5,700/800.
Said Isarescu: "In this period of turbulence the best thing is to maintain a free-floating system for the leu, and to use the exchange rate and the market as a safety valve." REUTER
